records.gloss: A psalm of David. YHWH [is] my shepherd; I will not lack.
pieces: A psalm of David. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is my shepherd; \q I will never be in need.

L.1: A psalm of David. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} [is] my shepherd; \q I will not lack [anything].

R.1: A song of David. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} takes care of me like a shepherd. \q I have everything I need.

decisions.choice: The title shares verse 1
decisions.reason: This psalm's title is short and the Hebrew counts it together with the first line as verse 1, so here the verse numbers are the same as in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: my shepherd: the one who leads, feeds and guards
decisions.reason: A shepherd lived with his flock, led it to grass and water and fought off wild animals. Kings were called shepherds of their people, and God is the shepherd of Israel (80:2; Genesis 48:15; Ezekiel 34:11-15). Here he is "my" shepherd.

decisions.choice: I will not lack: I have and will have all I need
decisions.reason: The verb (chaser) is the one used of Israel in the wilderness: "you have lacked nothing" (Deuteronomy 2:7). Its form covers the present and the future.

decisions.choice: takes care of me like a shepherd
decisions.reason: Readable makes the picture a comparison and says what a shepherd does (m2).

decisions.choice: song
decisions.reason: As in 3:1.

records.heading: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, my shepherd and host

records.source: בִּנְא֣וֹת דֶּ֭שֶׁא יַרְבִּיצֵ֑נִי עַל־מֵ֖י מְנֻח֣וֹת יְנַהֲלֵֽנִי׃
records.gloss: In pastures of fresh grass he makes me lie down; beside waters of rest he leads me.
pieces: He settles me down in meadows of fresh green grass; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} leads me gently to water where I can rest.

L.2: In pastures of fresh grass {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes me lie down; \q beside waters of rest {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} leads me.

R.2: He lets me rest in fields of soft green grass. \q He takes me to calm water where I can drink and rest.

decisions.choice: he leads me: guides with care, to water and rest
decisions.reason: The verb (nahal) is used of leading a flock gently to water and of caring for the weak on the way (Isaiah 40:11; 49:10).

decisions.choice: waters of rest: water where the flock can rest
decisions.reason: The word (menuchot) means resting places, rest; the water is a place to drink and lie down in peace.

decisions.choice: where I can drink
decisions.reason: Readable says what the water is for.

records.source: נַפְשִׁ֥י יְשׁוֹבֵ֑ב יַֽנְחֵ֥נִי בְמַעְגְּלֵי־צֶ֝֗דֶק לְמַ֣עַן שְׁמֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: My soul he brings back; he guides me in tracks of righteousness for the sake of his name.
pieces: He brings back my life \q and leads me in the tracks of what is right, \q true to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.

L.3: My soul {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brings back; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} guides me in tracks of righteousness \q for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.

R.3: He makes me strong again. \q He shows me the right way to walk. \q He does this because of who {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is.

decisions.choice: he brings back my soul: he gives me new life
alternatives: he brings me back (when I stray)
decisions.reason: To bring back the soul is to restore life and strength (19:8). The verb (shuv) can also mean to bring back a sheep that has strayed.

decisions.choice: tracks of righteousness: paths that are right
decisions.reason: The tracks (ma'gal) are worn paths. "Of righteousness" means paths that lead the right way, and also paths of living rightly; both are meant.

decisions.choice: for the sake of his name: because of who he is
decisions.reason: God acts to show what he is like and to keep his good name (Ezekiel 36:22).

decisions.choice: because of who he is
alternatives: for the sake of his name
decisions.reason: Readable says what the phrase means (m3).

records.source: גַּ֤ם כִּֽי־אֵלֵ֨ךְ בְּגֵ֪יא צַלְמָ֡וֶת לֹא־אִ֘ירָ֤א רָ֗ע כִּי־אַתָּ֥ה עִמָּדִ֑י שִׁבְטְךָ֥ וּ֝מִשְׁעַנְתֶּ֗ךָ הֵ֣מָּה יְנַֽחֲמֻֽנִי׃
records.gloss: Even when I walk in [a] valley of deep darkness, I will not fear harm, for you [are] with me; your rod and your staff, they comfort me.
pieces: Even if my path goes down through a valley of deepest darkness, I will not be afraid of any harm, \q because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are there with me; \q {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} rod and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} staff give me courage.

L.4: Even when I walk in a valley of deep darkness, I will not fear harm, \q for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [are] with me; \q {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} rod and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} staff, they comfort me.

R.4: Even when I go through a valley that is very dark and dangerous, I will not be afraid, \q because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are right there beside me. \q You guard me with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} club and guide me with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} staff, and that comforts me.

decisions.choice: deep darkness
decisions.reason: The word (tsalmavet) means deep, thick darkness (Job 10:21-22). It can also be read as two words, "shadow of death", which is how the ancient translations took it. Either way the valley is a place of danger where death is near.

decisions.choice: you are with me: the psalm turns to speak to God
decisions.reason: Until now the psalmist has spoken about the LORD; in the dark valley he speaks to him directly.

decisions.choice: rod and staff: a shepherd's weapon and walking stick
decisions.reason: The rod (shevet) was a club to drive off wild animals; the staff (mish'enet) a long stick to lean on and to guide the sheep. Both reassure the sheep that the shepherd is there.

decisions.choice: you guard me with your club and guide me with your staff
alternatives: your rod and your staff comfort me
decisions.reason: Readable says what each is for (m3).

records.source: תַּעֲרֹ֬ךְ לְפָנַ֨י׀שֻׁלְחָ֗ן נֶ֥גֶד צֹרְרָ֑י דִּשַּׁ֖נְתָּ בַשֶּׁ֥מֶן רֹ֝אשִׁ֗י כּוֹסִ֥י רְוָיָֽה׃
records.gloss: You arrange before me a table in front of my foes; you have refreshed with oil my head; my cup [is] overflowing.
pieces: You spread a meal before me while my enemies look on; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} refresh my head with oil, \q and my cup is full to the brim.

L.5: You set a table before me in front of my foes; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have refreshed my head with oil; \q my cup [is] overflowing.

R.5: You set out a feast for me, and my enemies have to watch. \q You pour oil on my head to honor me. \q You fill my cup until it spills over.

decisions.choice: a table before my foes: God as host
decisions.reason: The picture changes from shepherd to host. A host who welcomed a guest to his table was bound to protect him; the enemies can only watch.

decisions.choice: refreshed with oil: welcomed and honored
decisions.reason: The verb (dishen) means to make rich or fat, here to refresh with oil. Oil on the head was a mark of welcome and gladness for a guest (104:15; Luke 7:46), not the anointing of a king.

decisions.choice: my cup overflowing: more than enough
decisions.reason: The cup is the portion one is given (16:5); his runs over.

decisions.choice: to honor me
decisions.reason: Readable says what the oil means (m2).

records.source: אַ֤ךְ׀ט֤וֹב וָחֶ֣סֶד יִ֭רְדְּפוּנִי כָּל־יְמֵ֣י חַיָּ֑י וְשַׁבְתִּ֥י בְּבֵית־יְ֝הוָ֗ה לְאֹ֣רֶךְ יָמִֽים׃
records.gloss: Surely goodness and loyal love will pursue me all [the] days of my life, and I will return in [the] house of YHWH for length of days.
pieces: Goodness and loyal love will surely chase after me every day I live, \q and I will come home to the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for all my days to come.

L.6: Surely goodness and loyal love will pursue me all the days of my life, \q and I will return [to dwell] in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for length of days.

R.6: I am sure that goodness and faithful love will run after me every day of my life. \q And I will come back to live in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s house for as long as I live.

decisions.choice: pursue me: chase after me
decisions.reason: The verb (radaf) is usually used of enemies in pursuit (7:2). Here the enemies of verse 5 only watch, and God's goodness and love are what chase him.

decisions.choice: loyal love: chesed
decisions.reason: As in 21:8, love that keeps faith with a bond.

decisions.choice: I will return
alternatives: I will dwell (the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text has "I will return" (shavti), with "in the house" as if "to dwell" were understood. The ancient Greek translation read "I will dwell" (veyashavti), a very similar word. Either way he will be at home with God.

decisions.choice: for length of days: as long as I live
decisions.reason: Length of days is a long life (21:5).

decisions.choice: faithful love
decisions.reason: Readable says "faithful love" for chesed (m2).

decisions.choice: return (L); come home (B)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced follow the Hebrew text (m3); Readable says "come back to live", which keeps both senses.
